note: Family-level eval set for the aws-ai-* skills. Each eval targets one stage's distinctive, verifiable behavior; the with_skill run starts from the aws-ai-lifecycle router and follows its routing, the baseline answers from general AWS knowledge.

evals.name: assess-service-selection
evals.prompt: We're a mid-size insurance company. I want our internal support portal to answer employees' questions from our ~4,000 policy PDFs (they change a few times a year). My VP keeps saying 'just fine-tune a model on Bedrock', but I'm not sure. Which AWS service should we use, and do we actually need to fine-tune? Rough idea of what it'd cost to run?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Bedrock + RAG/Knowledge Base over fine-tuning with reasoning (data changes, cost), frames Bedrock-managed vs SageMaker-self-host as a trade-off, does not jump to code, requests no credentials.
expectations: Recommends RAG / a Knowledge Base over fine-tuning, with a stated reason
Frames a real managed-vs-self-hosted trade-off — names a self-hosted/SageMaker tier OR an instance-hour-vs-per-token cost axis (not just 'managed RAG')
Surfaces Amazon Q Business as the purpose-built managed-assistant option for an internal-document Q&A portal
Does not jump straight to writing implementation code
Does not ask for or use real AWS credentials

evals.name: design-agent-rag-iam
evals.prompt: Good news, we're going Bedrock + RAG for the insurance support assistant. Can you design it? Single agent or a few? What do we use for the vector store, where do the guardrails sit, and what IAM does the Lambda actually need to call the model?
evals.expected_output: Gives a single-vs-multi-agent recommendation with reasoning, names a vector store with a trade-off, places guardrails in the request path, and specifies least-privilege IAM including the inference-profile + foundation-model ARN pair.
expectations: Makes a single-vs-multi-agent recommendation with reasoning
Names a concrete vector store (OpenSearch / S3 Vectors / pgvector) with a trade-off
Places guardrails explicitly in the request path
Specifies least-privilege IAM and flags the need for BOTH foundation-model and inference-profile ARNs
Flags the tool-authorization boundary guardrails cannot cover (Cedar/Verified Permissions on tool calls, a read/write trust split, or PrivateLink aws:sourceVpce)

evals.name: build-converse-tool-loop
evals.prompt: Write me the Python (boto3) for a Bedrock tool-use loop - the model should be able to call a get_policy_status(policy_id) tool and then answer the user. We're on Claude Sonnet. Just the core loop is fine.
evals.expected_output: Uses the native Converse API (bedrock-runtime converse) with a toolConfig, handles stopReason tool_use by returning a toolResult that echoes toolUseId, loops to end_turn. Does NOT use invoke_model with the legacy completion body.
expectations: Uses the native Converse API (bedrock-runtime.converse), not invoke_model with a completion body

Does NOT use the legacy 

Human:/

Assistant: or max_tokens_to_sample completion format
Implements the tool-use loop: toolConfig, stopReason tool_use, a toolResult echoing toolUseId, loop to end_turn
Passes the model id as a parameter/constant rather than presenting a hard-coded id as permanent
Bakes in cross-stage discipline the baseline lacks — a dependency-injected client, the two-ARN IAM note, or a max-turns loop guard
Wires the boto3 client as an injected parameter (an offline-testable seam that pre-wires the validate-stage Stubber), not a module-level global

evals.name: deploy-cdk-two-arn
evals.prompt: Give me AWS CDK in Python to deploy this Bedrock agent (it calls Claude Sonnet) as a Lambda with the right Bedrock permissions.
evals.expected_output: CDK (aws-cdk-lib, Python) with a Lambda + execution role granting bedrock:InvokeModel on BOTH foundation-model/* and inference-profile/* ARNs (the two-ARN trap), and mentions offline cdk synth validation / no real deploy without approval.
expectations: Produces AWS CDK v2 Python (aws-cdk-lib) with a Lambda and an execution role
Grants bedrock:InvokeModel on BOTH a foundation-model ARN AND an inference-profile ARN (the two-ARN trap)
Requires validation discipline beyond 'cdk synth' — cfn-lint OR cdk-nag OR an explicit deploy gate / human confirmation

evals.name: validate-offline-stubber
evals.prompt: How do I unit-test this Bedrock agent offline? I do NOT want CI hitting a real AWS account. The code calls Converse and also invokes a SageMaker endpoint for a risk score.
evals.expected_output: Recommends botocore Stubber for bedrock-runtime (and sagemaker-runtime), notes moto cannot mock bedrock-runtime, uses moto for supporting infra, and reinforces offline-first with no real credentials in CI.
expectations: Recommends botocore Stubber for bedrock-runtime (and sagemaker-runtime) contract tests
Notes that moto cannot mock bedrock-runtime, so Stubber is required for it
Uses moto (or equivalent) for supporting infra / SageMaker control plane
Reinforces offline-first / no real credentials in CI

evals.name: router-where-to-start
evals.prompt: We want to add some GenAI to our AWS app but honestly have no idea where to start. What's the actual process/steps?
evals.expected_output: Routes to assessing the capability & selecting the service first (not code/deploy), lays out the assess -> design -> build -> deploy -> validate progression, and emphasizes offline-first + credential gating.
expectations: Starts by assessing the capability and selecting the AWS service (does not jump to code or deployment)
Lays out the stage progression assess -> design -> build -> deploy -> validate
Emphasizes offline-first and that real credentials are gated to the validate step
